newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters says NZ Dec current a/c data encouraging.
newsitem.headline: Peters says NZ Dec current a/c data encouraging.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer and Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters said on Thursday an improvement in the merchandise trade surplus for the third quarter in a row, revealed in December quarter balance of payments data, was "very encouraging".
"The government is keen to see this trend continue," Peters said through a spokesman.
"Today's figures confirm the government's view that the economy is on the right track."
Peters also noted that the current account deficit to GDP ratio, which came in a 4.2 percent for the year to December 31, was better than market expectations.
Statistics New Zealand earlier on Thursday said New Zealand's merchandise trade surlus was NZ$40 million in the December 1996 quarter, up from a $317 million deficit in the September 1996 quarter.
SNZ said the December quarter current account deficit was $1.29 billion and the December annual current account deficit was $3.91 billion.
